comment: Four rows cover projected call arguments, aggregate call results, residual call
publication, and divergence publication (D17.18). The build writes LLVM IR for
the focused module test. The stage compiles and runs the same test with the mutant.
Run this table in the Linux VM with the debug preset.
build: mkdir -p build/Linux/debug/mutate && build/Linux/debug/fort --std-dir build/Linux/debug/std -I src/fort -I test/fort/support -S -o build/Linux/debug/mutate/ownership_summary_call_publication_test.ll test/fort/ownership_summary_call_publication_test.ft

stages.name: call and publication summary module test
stages.command: python3 test/lang/run_tests.py --root test/fort --fort build/Linux/debug/fort --std-dir build/Linux/debug/std --cc /usr/bin/clang --target x86_64-linux-gnu --verify-ir -j 1 ownership_summary_call_publication

mutations.what: a projected copy argument remains unsupported
a non-owning aggregate call result remains unsupported
a residual call discards the observed cases at publication
a proved divergent call becomes an unknown call outcome
